paper.title: Selective migration and mortality by economic status in Lolland-Falster, Denmark, 1992–2018
paper.code_data_availability: Data availability (p. 8): "Data was extracted from the Danish Health Data Authority and Statistics Denmark. …

registers.role: sample frame, treatment (residency group) and outcome (death); individual-level data on all persons ever living in Denmark in the study period
treatment (economic status: self-supported vs publicly supported), from annual main income source

linkages: CPR data were merged with data from Statistics Denmark´s socioeconomic classification (SOCIO13) including data on annual main income source for 1991-2017
Individual-level register data accessed and linked through Statistics Denmark's research server

sample.universe: All people aged 30–64 years and living in Denmark at any time between 1992 and 2018
sample.unit_of_observation: person-year at risk, stratified into event-time tables by 5-year age-group, calendar period, sex, residency group and economic status (Rostgaard's method)
selection_rules: Aged 30–64 years: a given person contributed person-years only while he/she was 30–64 years old
Registered at a Danish address: a person belonged to the population in the rest of Denmark as long as he/she was registered with an address in Denmark outside Lolland-Falster

Lolland-Falster residents divided into long-term residents (lived continuously in Lolland-Falster the 10 years prior to the time-period) and in-migrants (moved to Lolland-Falster during the 10 years preceding the time-period or during the time-period), based on address history
A given person belonged to the last socioeconomic group in which he/she appeared in the register
If a person had missing data for SOCIO13 one year, they did not contribute person-years or deaths in the following year

Dynamic population: a person contributed person-years to a group from the point he/she fulfilled the criteria for the group until he/she no longer did, and could contribute to different residency groups in different time-periods

construction_notes: Lolland-Falster is defined as Lolland and Guldborgsund municipalities
Residency group is based on the person's address history during the previous 10 years; in a sensitivity analysis, 20 years instead of 10

A long-term resident remained in that group until death, emigration or end of follow-up; a long-term resident who moved outside Lolland-Falster and back again during a time-period became an in-migrant
The long-term residents and the in-migrants together constitute the total Lolland-Falster population

Economic status is a dichotomous variable built from the 20 mutually exclusive annual SOCIO13 categories, measured as the status held during the majority of the previous year; in a sensitivity analysis, the status three years before (not possible for 1992–1999, as SOCIO13 data are available only from 1991 onwards)

Self-supported = employees, self-employed persons and their assisting spouses; publicly supported = people on public transfer payment: non-old age pensioners, old age pensioners, unemployment benefit, early retirement scheme, sickness benefits, cash benefits or adult education support (Appendix Table 1)

Mortality rate ratios estimated by Poisson regression on event-time tables with person-time as offset, adjusted for 5-year age-group and (for the total population) sex; self-supported people in the rest of Denmark are the reference group in each time-period
Analyses run separately for men, for women and for the total population, and separately for the three time-periods
All analysis were made in SAS 9.4 and graphics were made in R 4.0.3 at a research server in Statistics Denmark

claims.statement: Among people aged 30–64 years in 2010–2018 (men and women combined), self-supported people in Lolland-Falster (long-term residents and in-migrants combined) had an all-cause mortality rate higher than that of self-supported people in the rest of Denmark (MRR 1.42, 95% CI 1.31–1.53).

treatment.label: Self-supported people in Lolland-Falster (long-term residents and in-migrants combined) (vs self-supported people in the rest of Denmark)

register_source.value: Central Population Register (CPR): sex, date of birth, address history, emigration and immigration; Statistics Denmark's socioeconomic classification SOCIO13: annual main income source, 1991–2017

definition.value: Mutually exclusive residency x economic-status group of the person-years at risk. Residency group is based on the person's address history during the previous 10 years: long-term residents had lived continuously in Lolland-Falster (Lolland and Guldborgsund municipalities) for the 10 years prior to the time-period; in-migrants had moved to Lolland-Falster during the 10 years preceding the time-period or during the time-period; everyone registered at a Danish address outside Lolland-Falster belongs to the rest of Denmark. Economic status is a dichotomous variable built from the 20 mutually exclusive annual SOCIO13 categories, indicating whether the person was economically self-supported (employees, self-employed and their assisting spouses) or publicly supported (non-old age pensioners, old age pensioners, unemployment benefit, early retirement scheme, sickness benefits, cash benefits or adult education support) during the majority of the previous year.

timing.value: Residency group from the address history of the previous 10 years (and updated within the time-period); economic status from the SOCIO13 status held during the majority of the previous year

outcome.label: All-cause death, expressed as a mortality rate ratio (MRR)

register_source.value: Central Population Register (CPR): date of death

definition.value: All-cause death. Deaths and person-years at risk were stratified into event-time tables by 5-year age-group, sex, residency group, economic status and calendar period, and the mortality rate ratio (MRR) with 95% CI was estimated by Poisson regression with the person-time as offset, adjusted for 5-year age-group and (in the total population) sex, with self-supported people in the rest of Denmark as the reference (MRR = 1).

timing.value: Deaths occurring during 2010–2018 while the person was aged 30–64 years and registered at a Danish address

units.value: mortality rate ratio; reference = self-supported people in the rest of Denmark in the same time-period (MRR = 1), adjusted for 5-year age-group and sex

estimand.target_population: Person-years aged 30–64 years contributed in 2010–2018 by self-supported people in Lolland-Falster (long-term residents and in-migrants combined), relative to person-years of self-supported people in the rest of Denmark in the same period
estimand.formal_query: MRR = rate(death | group = exposure, 5-year age-group, sex) / rate(death | group = self-supported, rest of Denmark, same strata) — an associational rate ratio, not a do-expression

population.description: People aged 30–64 years living in Denmark at any time in 2010–2018; person-years counted while aged 30–64 and registered at a Danish address
population.region: Denmark; Lolland-Falster (Lolland and Guldborgsund municipalities) vs the rest of Denmark
subgroups_defined: the rest of the Danish population
population.selection: Total register population; a person contributed person-years to a group from the point in time he/she fulfilled the criteria for the group until he/she no longer did, only while aged 30–64 years and registered at a Danish address, and contributed no person-years or deaths in a year following a year with missing SOCIO13 data

identification.source_of_variation: None exogenous: observed differences in death rates between mutually exclusive residency x economic-status groups of the whole Danish register population, adjusted for 5-year age-group and sex

key_assumptions.assumption: Address history, vital status and annual economic status are completely and correctly recorded for the whole Danish population in the nationwide registers, so that person-years and deaths are allocated to the right group
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper presents the nationwide, high-quality Danish register data, already validated by Statistics Denmark before release for research, as a strength; no validation test of its own

key_assumptions.assumption: The comparison is adjusted for 5-year age-group and sex only; no other characteristic is controlled for, so the MRR describes the mortality difference between the groups as they are, not a confounding-free effect

Deaths are Poisson distributed given the person-time in each age-group x sex x residency x economic-status x period stratum, with differences in follow-up time handled by an offset and a constant rate within strata
key_assumptions.supported_by: Asserted as the natural model for count data; not tested

key_assumptions.assumption: A person contributes person-years only while aged 30–64 years and present at a Danish address, so the population is dynamic and conditioned on survival into, and residence during, the time-period
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated construction rule; no test

implies_edges.from: Sample inclusion: contributing person-years only while aged 30–64 and registered at a Danish address

key_assumptions.assumption: Person-years and deaths in a year following a year with missing SOCIO13 data are dropped, so the analysed person-time is conditioned on having an observed economic status in the preceding year
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated exclusion rule; the paper reports no analysis of who is dropped

implies_edges.from: Sample inclusion: non-missing SOCIO13 in the preceding year

threats_discussed: Mortality rates of people on public support may be inflated by deaths in previously self-supported people being on e.g. sickness benefit towards the end of life
Poor health is in some instances a precondition for eligibility for public support in working-age, so the association between public support and death may reflect selection by illness
A crude dichotomous categorisation of economic status that ignores mortality differences across occupations among the self-supported and between benefit types among the publicly supported
A generally negative health selection of people moving to Lolland-Falster, independent of economic status
Changes in living circumstances (break-up with partners, conflicts with neighbors, other difficulties in life) that could not be included
robustness_checks: Residency categorised by address history 20 years instead of 10 years before each time-period (Appendix Table 3): similar results as the main analysis

Economic status categorised by the annual status three years before instead of one year (Appendix Table 4): the excess mortality of publicly supported people decreased slightly, but the relative difference between Lolland-Falster and the rest of Denmark, between in-migrants and long-term residents, and across time-periods persisted; not possible for 1992–1999 because SOCIO13 data start in 1991
unresolved_confounders: Other changes in living circumstances like break-up with partners, conflicts with neighbors or other difficulties in life that we could not include in the present study
Inequalities in mortality across occupations within the group of self-supported people
Differences in mortality within the publicly supported group between those on temporary unemployment benefit and those on permanent non-old age pension
Whether the excess mortality reflects a generally negative health selection of movers to Lolland-Falster independent of economic status

estimator.value: Poisson regression on event-time tables (person-time offset), giving a mortality rate ratio with 95% CI; SAS 9.4

estimation.specification: Deaths regressed on indicators for the mutually exclusive residency x economic-status groups with person-years as offset, adjusted for 5-year age-group and sex; self-supported people in the rest of Denmark are the reference group in each time-period; estimated separately for each of the three time-periods. The paper prints no estimating equation.

sample_n.value: 289,617 person-years and 680 deaths in the exposure group; 16,773,066 person-years and 25,041 deaths in the reference group (self-supported, rest of Denmark)

source_table.value: Table 2, panel 2010–2018, Total, Self-supported block, MRR column, row 'Lolland-Falster'

heterogeneity.finding: Compared with the rest of Denmark, we found an excess mortality in Lolland-Falster within each of the economic status and residency groups, though stronger for in-migrants than for long-term residents.
The MRR trends were similar for men and women.

For the self-supported group in Lolland-Falster, the excess mortality as compared with that of self-supported people in the rest of Denmark emerged over time for long-term residents and was present for in-migrants in all time-periods

definition.value: Mutually exclusive residency x economic-status group of the person-years at risk. definition.value: Mutually exclusive residency x economic-status group of the person-years at risk. claims.statement: Among people aged 30–64 years in 2010–2018 (women), all long-term residents of Lolland-Falster, irrespective of economic status, had an all-cause mortality rate higher than that of self-supported people in the rest of Denmark (MRR 2.77, 95% CI 2.56–2.99).

definition.value: Mutually exclusive residency x economic-status group of the person-years at risk. Residency group is based on the person's address history during the previous 10 years: long-term residents had lived continuously in Lolland-Falster (Lolland and Guldborgsund municipalities) for the 10 years prior to the time-period; in-migrants had moved to Lolland-Falster during the 10 years preceding the time-period or during the time-period; everyone registered at a Danish address outside Lolland-Falster belongs to the rest of Denmark. Economic status is a dichotomous variable built from the 20 mutually exclusive annual SOCIO13 categories, indicating whether the person was economically self-supported (employees, self-employed and their assisting spouses) or publicly supported (non-old age pensioners, old age pensioners, unemployment benefit, early retirement scheme, sickness benefits, cash benefits or adult education support) during the majority of the previous year.

timing.value: Residency group from the address history of the previous 10 years (and updated within the time-period); economic status from the SOCIO13 status held during the majority of the previous year

definition.value: Mutually exclusive residency x economic-status group of the person-years at risk. Residency group is based on the person's address history during the previous 10 years: long-term residents had lived continuously in Lolland-Falster (Lolland and Guldborgsund municipalities) for the 10 years prior to the time-period; in-migrants had moved to Lolland-Falster during the 10 years preceding the time-period or during the time-period; everyone registered at a Danish address outside Lolland-Falster belongs to the rest of Denmark. definition.value: Mutually exclusive residency x economic-status group of the person-years at risk. Residency group is based on the person's address history during the previous 10 years: long-term residents had lived continuously in Lolland-Falster (Lolland and Guldborgsund municipalities) for the 10 years prior to the time-period; in-migrants had moved to Lolland-Falster during the 10 years preceding the time-period or during the time-period; everyone registered at a Danish address outside Lolland-Falster belongs to the rest of Denmark. claims.statement: Among people aged 30–64 years in 1992–1999 (men), self-supported in-migrants to Lolland-Falster had an all-cause mortality rate higher than that of self-supported people in the rest of Denmark (MRR 1.32, 95% CI 1.06–1.63).

register_source.value: Central Population Register (CPR): sex, date of birth, address history, emigration and immigration; Statistics Denmark's socioeconomic classification SOCIO13: annual main income source, 1991–2017

definition.value: Mutually exclusive residency x economic-status group of the person-years at risk. Residency group is based on the person's address history during the previous 10 years: long-term residents had lived continuously in Lolland-Falster (Lolland and Guldborgsund municipalities) for the 10 years prior to the time-period; in-migrants had moved to Lolland-Falster during the 10 years preceding the time-period or during the time-period; everyone registered at a Danish address outside Lolland-Falster belongs to the rest of Denmark. Economic status is a dichotomous variable built from the 20 mutually exclusive annual SOCIO13 categories, indicating whether the person was economically self-supported (employees, self-employed and their assisting spouses) or publicly supported (non-old age pensioners, old age pensioners, unemployment benefit, early retirement scheme, sickness benefits, cash benefits or adult education support) during the majority of the previous year.

timing.value: Residency group from the address history of the previous 10 years (and updated within the time-period); economic status from the SOCIO13 status held during the majority of the previous year

definition.value: All-cause death. treatment.label: Publicly supported people in Lolland-Falster (long-term residents and in-migrants combined) (vs self-supported people in the rest of Denmark)

register_source.value: Central Population Register (CPR): sex, date of birth, address history, emigration and immigration; Statistics Denmark's socioeconomic classification SOCIO13: annual main income source, 1991–2017

definition.value: Mutually exclusive residency x economic-status group of the person-years at risk. Residency group is based on the person's address history during the previous 10 years: long-term residents had lived continuously in Lolland-Falster (Lolland and Guldborgsund municipalities) for the 10 years prior to the time-period; in-migrants had moved to Lolland-Falster during the 10 years preceding the time-period or during the time-period; everyone registered at a Danish address outside Lolland-Falster belongs to the rest of Denmark. Economic status is a dichotomous variable built from the 20 mutually exclusive annual SOCIO13 categories, indicating whether the person was economically self-supported (employees, self-employed and their assisting spouses) or publicly supported (non-old age pensioners, old age pensioners, unemployment benefit, early retirement scheme, sickness benefits, cash benefits or adult education support) during the majority of the previous year.

timing.value: Residency group from the address history of the previous 10 years (and updated within the time-period); economic status from the SOCIO13 status held during the majority of the previous year

outcome.label: All-cause death, expressed as a mortality rate ratio (MRR)

register_source.value: Central Population Register (CPR): date of death

definition.value: All-cause death. Deaths and person-years at risk were stratified into event-time tables by 5-year age-group, sex, residency group, economic status and calendar period, and the mortality rate ratio (MRR) with 95% CI was estimated by Poisson regression with the person-time as offset, adjusted for 5-year age-group and (in the total population) sex, with self-supported people in the rest of Denmark as the reference (MRR = 1).

timing.value: Deaths occurring during 1992–1999 while the person was aged 30–64 years and registered at a Danish address

units.value: mortality rate ratio; reference = self-supported people in the rest of Denmark in the same time-period (MRR = 1), adjusted for 5-year age-group

estimand.target_population: Person-years aged 30–64 years contributed in 1992–1999 by publicly supported people in Lolland-Falster (long-term residents and in-migrants combined) (women only), relative to person-years of self-supported people in the rest of Denmark in the same period
estimand.formal_query: MRR = rate(death | group = exposure, 5-year age-group) / rate(death | group = self-supported, rest of Denmark, same strata) — an associational rate ratio, not a do-expression

population.description: People aged 30–64 years living in Denmark at any time in 1992–1999, women only; person-years counted while aged 30–64 and registered at a Danish address

unresolved_confounders: Other changes in living circumstances like break-up with partners, conflicts with neighbors or other difficulties in life that we could not include in the present study

definition.value: Mutually exclusive residency x economic-status group of the person-years at risk. Residency group is based on the person's address history during the previous 10 years: long-term residents had lived continuously in Lolland-Falster (Lolland and Guldborgsund municipalities) for the 10 years prior to the time-period; in-migrants had moved to Lolland-Falster during the 10 years preceding the time-period or during the time-period; everyone registered at a Danish address outside Lolland-Falster belongs to the rest of Denmark. Economic status is a dichotomous variable built from the 20 mutually exclusive annual SOCIO13 categories, indicating whether the person was economically self-supported (employees, self-employed and their assisting spouses) or publicly supported (non-old age pensioners, old age pensioners, unemployment benefit, early retirement scheme, sickness benefits, cash benefits or adult education support) during the majority of the previous year.
